title: Sensing stretch
objective: Explain how visceral afferents transduce mechanical stretch and what defines the adequate stimulus.

steps.title: Distension is the signal
steps.body: For a hollow organ, the meaningful mechanical event is **distension** — the wall stretching as it fills. Muscle-embedded afferents transduce that stretch, in large part through **[[Piezo2]]**, the same mechanically-activated channel used for touch. Cutting the wall barely registers; stretching it does.

steps.prompt: What is the 'adequate stimulus' for most gut mechanosensory afferents?
options: A fine surgical cut to the lining
A light brush across the mucosa
Heat applied to the outer wall
steps.explanation: Hollow-organ afferents are mostly tuned to stretch — the signal that matters for a filling, moving tube. Cutting and burning barely register; light mucosal stroking drives only a subset (mucosal afferents).

variants.setup: A balloon is slowly inflated inside the colon.
variants.prompt: Why does this drive the afferents so well?
options: It compresses vessels and makes the wall ischemic
It scrapes the lining, like a small cut
variants.reveal: Inflation stretches the wall, the adequate mechanical stimulus for these afferents.

steps.setup: You delete Piezo2 specifically from sensory neurons and then test gut mechanics.
options: Reduced stretch-evoked firing and altered GI transit
Loss of the capsaicin (TRPV1) response but normal stretch
No gut effect, since Piezo2 only serves skin touch
steps.reveal: Piezo2 is a principal stretch transducer here; removing it blunts mechanosensation and shifts transit. It wouldn't touch the chemical (TRPV1/capsaicin) response, which is a separate pathway.

options: Reduces stretch responses and alters transit
Boosts stretch responses above the normal level
variants.explanation: Piezo2 transduces stretch; its loss blunts mechanosensation, sparing chemical sensing.

sources.note: PIEZO2 in somatosensory neurons controls GI transit; visceral stretch transduction.
DRG subtypes tile the distal colon by force threshold; endings in defined wall layers.
